target_customer: Consumer brands, mostly Korean beauty and e-commerce brands, that pay for AI run growth and operations
problem: Consumer brands are limited by human hiring and coordination speed. Light Anchor runs ads, storefronts, AI search visibility and research with AI agents on a shared platform and also operates its own AI run brands.
business_model: Performance fee of 5 to 15 percent of revenue the agents create, with pilot first and no retainer (company site)
product_category: AI native growth agency and AI run consumer brands

founders.name: Chase Kim
founders.background_notes: YC page says founders led Sendbird's AI agent product and forward deployment teams, respectively, without mapping each one.

founders.name: Sangha Park
founders.background_notes: Korean press names the CEO as Park Sangha (박상하) and a co-founder Kim Youngdo (김영도); the English names are not mapped in any source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that run ads and storefronts across Meta, Google, TikTok and Amazon are integration heavy but built on existing platforms and models.

defensibility.rationale: Shared platform learning across brands could compound, but agency style services are easy to imitate.

market_need_then: The company claims eight client brands and sample reports showing weekly sales for one serum brand, all self reported; Korean e-commerce brands entering global markets supply demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious: building the AI native P&G

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Korean press (Byline Network, Venture Square) and RuntimeWire, mostly about funding and the product.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press coverage but no sign of brand pull yet; unrelated companies named Light or Anchor appear in searches.

outcome_analysis: Light Anchor is a Spring 2026 company that raised pre-YC seed money from Krew Capital and ASQ and a YC investment, and runs AI agents for several brands. No outcome yet. Risks are agency style services that scale with revenue share and dependence on ad platforms.
notes: The February 2026 round stage is not stated by the source (called the first investment), so it is recorded as other with no amount. One aggregator shows a $12M total and a Korean listing describes a different data operations product, which conflicts with the YC page; both are unverified and ignored. The competitor search returned only generic agentic commerce coverage, so the list is empty. The YC page says 10 brands, the TL;DR says one flagship plus experiments, and the site lists eight.
